lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fabio Luiz Segura | Lesson 17 -- Numbers That Move People
lesson.grammar_point: fronted adverbials and despite versus although for presenting data

listenings.text: Good morning. Three numbers from the overnight data, and then we'll go to questions. First, over the last fiscal year, cross-border payment volume in the region grew by about eleven percent. That's slower than the year before, and the main headwind was the strong dollar. Second, despite that, uptake of instant cross-border products more than doubled. But that was from a very small base, so the growth rate looks spectacular and the absolute numbers are still modest. And third, as of this quarter, three of the five largest banks in the region are running pilots. In my view, that's the real inflection point. When the large banks scale up, the rest of the market usually follows within two years.

When a bank shows me a huge addressable market, I am polite, but I don't write it down. Every market is enormous on a slide. What I write down is the run rate, and how it has changed over the last six months. A small run rate that grows every month tells me more than a big addressable market. The second thing I listen for is honesty about the headwinds. If the speaker tells me there are none, I stop listening. And the third thing is context. A number without a comparison means nothing to me. Fourteen percent, compared to what? If you tell me it is twice the growth of the economy, now I understand, and now I remember it.
